test_title: PYST 02: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Were you laughing at the poor masses?

options.text: Are the poor masses being laughed at by you?
Were the poor masses being laughed at by you?
Have the poor masses been laughed at by you?
Had the masses been laughed at by you?

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Were you laughing at the poor masses?"
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the poor masses" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "were laughing" to "were being laughed" (past continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "you."
 
• Ensure the question form is maintained.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Were the poor masses being laughed at by you?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Are the poor masses being laughed at by you?" – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"Have the poor masses been laughed at by you?" – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"Had the masses been laughed at by you?" – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
